name: Cessna Citation II / V / Ultra / Encore / Bravo
summary: Long-running family of straight-wing light/midsize Citations; the Army and Marine Corps fly the Ultra/Encore as the UC-35 for staff and priority transport.

wings: Low, straight (unswept) wing with a long span
engines: Two Pratt & Whitney Canada JT15D/PW530/PW535 turbofans in pods on the rear fuselage
fuselage: Slender fuselage with a long tapered nose and small rounded-square windows
Citation V/Ultra/Encore are a slight stretch with an extra window
tail: Horizontal stabilizer mounted low on the tail cone with pronounced dihedral (not a T-tail)
Tall swept fin with a dorsal fillet

tellTales: Straight unswept wing on a twinjet whose tailplane sits low on the tail cone
Tailplane angled upward with strong dihedral below a tall swept fin
Long slim nose and small windows on a slender tube fuselage

confusedWith.howToTell: The Citation II/V family has its tailplane low on the tail cone with dihedral; the CJ series has a T-tail.
The Citation II/V has a slim, low fuselage; the Excel/XLS has a noticeably deeper, fatter stand-up cabin on the same style of straight wing.
The Citation II/V is much longer with more windows; the Mustang is a tiny four-to-five-seat jet with only a few windows.
The Citation I is the shorter, smaller original with a shorter-span wing and fewer cabin windows; the Citation II is longer with a longer-span wing.
